newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia capital lights up in time for Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Liberia capital lights up in time for Christmas.

text.p: Liberia's battered capital, deprived of electricity for much of the civil war, has power supplies once again -- and just in time for Christmas.
The Liberia Electricity Company switched the power back on Thursday, pledging to supply electricity to key districts of the city for the next six months.
"The electricity we're supplying now is the result of Mr Charles Taylor's cash donation of $20,000 last month to us," its managing director, Samuel Nathaniel Burnette, said.
He said Taylor, who launched the civil war on Christmas Eve 1989, asked the company to make electricity available to the city before Christmas.
Taylor has already announced his candidacy for elections envisaged by May under the latest peace plan.
Monrovia residents last received a power supply in 1992 before a second failed attempt by Taylor to capture the city.
The war has killed well over 150,000 people. West African leaders brokered the latest peace deal and have threatened sanctions against any warlord derailing it. Much depends on disarmament.
Disarmament has begun but progress has been erratic with fighters in some places refusing to hand over their weapons. They have until January 31 to comply under the peace plan.
The United Nations has complained about ethnic Krahn fighters, who were at the centre of fighting in Monrovia in April and May, harassing their staff in the south west.
